structure: Oregon 2024 Social Science Standards, K-12 single PDF (89 pp). Front matter (pp1-8): title, TOC, revisions, domain/concept code tables (Civics C, Geography G, Economics E, History H), ten Essential Disciplinary Practices (EDP) table with explanations, Transformative SEL and Inclusive Social Science notes. Then grade sections in order: K, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6/7 (combined), 8, and High School (HS). Each grade section starts with one block giving title/focus plus a narrative paragraph(s), then the 'Essential Disciplinary Practices' heading and a table repeating the ten practices (extracted as wrapped column fragments, one cell per line fragment), then one table per domain headed 'Civics (g.C)', 'Geography (g.G)', 'Economics (g.E)', 'History (g.H)'. Domain tables have columns Concept | Code | Standard | 'Examples include, but not limited to:'; the Concept strand name spans several rows (multi-line text plus abbreviation like (C.PI)) in the first column, the code is grade.domain.concept.number (e.g. 4.C.PI.1, 6/7.G.MM.3, HS.C.IR.8), and the bulleted examples sit in the last column of the same row. Column indices shift (C1-C4 or C2-C5) between tables/pages, so the Examples column was taken from the header cell 'Examples include...' of each table; tables continued on later pages with no header row inherit the previous table's example column. Only HS has course-style sections: Civics (HS.C), Geography (HS.G), Economics (HS.E) are domain tables (labeled course null, grades 9-12), while 'US History (HS.US) 1865-Present' and 'World History (HS.WR) (1789-Present)' are labeled as courses. Concept cells, codes and standard statements = standards; example column cells = examples; grade overview narratives = examples.
